papers.title: Corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis control wakefulness in physiological and stressful conditions in mice.
keywords: bed nucleus of the stria terminalis
papers.summary: Optogenetic activation of CRH-expressing neurons in the BNST rapidly shifted mice from NREM sleep to wakefulness and also from REM sleep, while chemogenetic activation increased wakefulness and inhibition decreased wakefulness and alleviated stress-induced heightened wakefulness. The study identifies BNST CRH neurons as key regulators of wakefulness under physiological and stressful conditions.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Induces Glial Dysfunction, Synaptic Loss, Metabolic Imbalance, and Cognitive Impairment in 12-Month-Old Mice: Protective Effects of D30.
papers.summary: In 12-month-old mice, long-term sleep deprivation (LSD) caused sustained reductions in dendritic spine density, synaptic protein levels, and microglial/astrocytic morphological complexity, along with disrupted mitochondrial metabolism involving the TCA cycle, AMPK signaling, and lipid homeostasis. Treatment with D30 ameliorated these deficits, preserving glial homeostasis, restoring synaptic protein expression and spine density, rebalancing systemic metabolism, and improving cognitive performance.

papers.title: Atlas-Based Electrical Source Imaging for Mouse EEG: Application to an Fmr1 Knockout Model.
papers.summary: The authors developed an atlas-based electrical source imaging pipeline for 30-channel mouse EEG, validated it against simulated dipoles with best performance using a region-of-interest source space, ellipsoid head model, and sLORETA (mean error 0.93 mm superficial, 5.08 mm deep). Applied to Fmr1 knockout mice, it localized elevated gamma power to six parcels, with three in both low and high gamma bands, and detected regional variations in delta, theta, high gamma, and aperiodic parameters.

papers.title: Editorial: Criticality: a novel brain metric associated with sleep that may elucidate sleep's influence on adolescent depression.
papers.journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
papers.summary: This editorial proposes brain criticality, an EEG measure of neural dynamics and information processing capacity, as a novel mechanistic lens linking sleep disturbance to adolescent depression. It outlines how depression-related deviations from criticality could reflect a shifted set point, altered drift, or failed reset, each predicting distinct clinical presentations, and highlights the immediate translational potential of criticality metrics from existing EEG data.

papers.title: Offline generative network reconfiguration guides insight-like accelerated learning by assimilation into schema in rats.
papers.summary: In rats learning a cross-modal associative task, a mental schema enabled rapid within-day acquisition of novel cue-place associations. Hippocampal-medial prefrontal ensemble recordings revealed that offline generative network reconfiguration during post-encoding sleep/rest predicted insight-like accelerated learning, and hippocampal ripple disruption prevented it.

papers.title: Seasonal variations in the polysomnographic sleep/wake cycle and activity/rest pattern in the dromedary camel (Camelus dromedarius).
papers.journal: Journal of comparative physiology. B, Biochemical, systemic, and environmental physiology
papers.summary: Polysomnographic and behavioral recordings in six captive female dromedaries across four seasons showed seasonal changes in vigilance states, with total sleep time higher in winter (4.8 h) than summer (3.6 h) and wakefulness lower in winter (52.9%) than summer (59.8%). The findings link longer winter dark phase to increased sleep duration, supporting photoperiodic regulation of activity/rest and sleep/wake cycles.

papers.title: Fast-ripples are emergent properties of neuronal networks
papers.summary: Combining in silico simulations, neuronal cultures, rodent epilepsy models, and human microwire recordings, this study found that most fast-ripples (250-500 Hz) reflect stochastic network activity rather than distinctly generated pathological entities. Fast-ripple incidence exceeded chance in awake rodents and humans but not in neuronal cultures or sleeping rodents, suggesting their higher prevalence in epileptogenic tissue is primarily due to increased excitation and/or neural synchronization.

papers.title: Brain network dynamics in the wake-sleep transition reorganize according to task engagement.
papers.summary: Using EEG-fMRI in individuals fluctuating between alert and drowsy states during active or passive auditory tasks, this study found that actively maintaining task engagement during decreasing alertness increased long-range frontoparietal synchronization and auditory cortex synchronization, while passive listening led to increased parietal and thalamocortical synchronization. The results suggest flexible functional reorganization when alertness declines but cognitive processes persist.

papers.title: An open-set learning framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: The study proposes a two-stage open-set learning framework for EEG sleep stage classification, using an adaptive Gaussian method with quantile thresholds to separate known and unknown samples and a trainable decision boundary OpenMax module to refine classification. Experiments on three public EEG datasets showed strong performance for known sleep stages and effective detection of unknown categories, improving open-set recognition.

papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization.
papers.journal: Digest of technical papers. Symposium on VLSI Technology
papers.summary: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation that performs low-noise EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A memory reuse technique and runtime dynamic quantization reduced model size by 3.88× with only 0.28% accuracy loss, achieving 98.3% sensitivity for deep sleep detection.

papers.title: Reduced sensorimotor lactate concentration and improved sleep efficiency following resistance training in older adults.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of 12 weeks of explosive lower-body resistance training on sensorimotor lactate and N-acetylaspartate levels, sleep architecture, and sleep quality in older adults. Resistance training significantly reduced resting lactate concentration, improved objective sleep efficiency, and prolonged total sleep time compared to a control group, suggesting benefits for sleep and neural oxidative metabolism.

papers.title: Polygenic score for sleep duration in relation to the risk of Alzheimer's disease: results from the UK biobank.
papers.summary: Using wearable-derived sleep duration GWAS in 77,770 UK Biobank participants, the authors generated polygenic scores and tested their association with Alzheimer's disease in 264,746 independent participants (1,451 cases). The highest fifth of genetically predicted sleep duration (about 15 min/day longer sleep) had lower Alzheimer's disease risk (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.67-0.94).

papers.title: Modifiable Physiological Factors Associated With Human Glymphatic and Interstitial Fluid Dynamics-Related Measures: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped human evidence on non-pharmacological modifiable physiological factors associated with glymphatic and interstitial fluid dynamics-related measures, including 105 studies from 4134 records. Sleep quality/architecture/insomnia (n=45) and blood pressure/hypertension (n=25) were the largest domains, but evidence was dominated by observational studies and surrogate outcomes.

papers.title: Longitudinal association of self-reported restless sleep and duration with motoric cognitive risk syndrome in Chinese older adults: Evidence from CHARLS.
papers.summary: This longitudinal analysis of 3,600 Chinese older adults in CHARLS examined self-reported restless sleep and sleep duration in relation to incident motoric cognitive risk syndrome over a mean 3.63 years. Frequent restless sleep (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.06-2.76) and short sleep duration <6 h/night (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.03-2.27) were associated with higher MCR risk, with the combination showing HR 2.00.

papers.title: Digital motor and cognitive variability as early markers of the prodromal Parkinsons disease spectrum
papers.summary: Remote digital motor and cognitive tests in PD-risk-stratified prodromal cohorts found baseline motor/cognitive impairment in PSG-confirmed iRBD and intermediate deficits in hyposmic pRBD, with no linear motor decline but widespread performance variability. Cognitive variability was elevated in PSG-iRBD and hyposmic pRBD, and visit-specific motor instability occurred across prodromal cohorts on the BRAIN test.

papers.title: The hypoxic burden algorithm: an integrated index for assessing intermittent hypoxia in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea-a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort of 115 children with suspected obstructive sleep apnea compared a new hypoxic burden algorithm against conventional nocturnal hypoxic metrics from polysomnography. Hypoxic burden showed the strongest correlation with obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (r=0.801) and the best diagnostic performance (AUC 0.888) among the assessed indices.

papers.title: No Influence of Sleep Quality and Chronotype on the Effects of Mental Fatigue: Evidence From an Exploratory Analysis.
papers.summary: This exploratory analysis tested whether sleep quality and chronotype moderate subjective, cognitive, and physical responses to a 45-minute Stroop-induced mental fatigue task versus a control documentary. Most outcomes showed no meaningful moderation, though sleep quality (p=0.028) and chronotype (p=0.002) influenced general subjective mental fatigue, and chronotype groups differed in sleepiness (p<0.001).

papers.title: Bidirectional EEG Neurofeedback of Sensorimotor Beta Oscillations Reveals Asymmetric Modulation and Strategy-Dependent Learning.
papers.summary: This exploratory study assessed the ability of healthy participants to bidirectionally modulate sensorimotor beta power using EEG neurofeedback in a double-blind sham-controlled within-subjects design. Thirteen participants successfully decreased beta activity, three successfully increased it, and two demonstrated bidirectional control; real neurofeedback success was significantly higher than sham when sham was first, indicating a transfer learning effect.

papers.title: Preoperative sleep-related problems and their association with postoperative agitation, pain, and early postoperative sleep-related problems in children undergoing orthopedic surgery.
papers.summary: In 104 children undergoing orthopedic surgery, preoperative sleep-related problems were positively correlated with higher postoperative agitation and pain scores and with increased postoperative sleep problems, while agitation and pain decreased by postoperative day 1.

papers.title: The protective role of resilience-related strength in the association between sleep reactivity and insomnia symptoms among young Chinese male university students: a moderated network approach.
papers.summary: Among 1,122 young Chinese male university students, sleep reactivity was positively associated with insomnia symptoms, and the resilience dimension Strength negatively associated with and moderated this relationship, with moderated network analysis localizing the moderation to specific sleep reactivity-insomnia links involving interpersonal conflict and public speaking.

papers.title: Reduced Motor Preparation and Altered EEG Signatures of Prediction in Autistic Adults.
papers.summary: In a preregistered EEG experiment, autistic adults showed less behavioral benefit from high-probability auditory cues and a reduced late CNV motor preparatory potential compared with IQ- and language-matched non-autistic controls, alongside shallower 1 Hz ramping potentials and reduced posterior phase entrainment.

papers.title: Pluripotency and Transcriptional Pausing Disrupt Circadian Rhythms to Facilitate the Enrichment of Cancer Stem Cells
papers.summary: Carboplatin-treated triple-negative breast cancer cells lost circadian rhythms and enriched cancer stem cells, and genetic circadian clock ablation alone promoted cancer stem cell formation and tumorsphere/tumor generation; OCT4 disrupted circadian gene expression, and restoring rhythms in Oct4-deficient cells impaired tumorsphere formation and reduced cancer stem cells in mouse tumors.

papers.title: Serial amplitude-integrated electroencephalography trajectories and brain-injury-associated functional immaturity in extremely preterm infants.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study characterized postmenstrual-age-specific Burdjalov maturation trajectories in 156 extremely preterm infants using 723 serial amplitude-integrated EEG recordings. Infants with major brain injury scored on average 1.45 points lower at 32 weeks PMA, with persistent differences across PMA windows, but the study cautions against interpreting unstable linear interactions as biological recovery.

papers.title: Circadian immunoregulation in cutaneous wound healing: from immune cell temporal heterogeneity to chronotherapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how circadian rhythms regulate immune cell recruitment, activation, and resolution during cutaneous wound healing, focusing on neutrophil trafficking and macrophage temporal heterogeneity. It discusses how circadian disruption in conditions like diabetes, aging, and sleep disturbance may desynchronize immune responses and promote chronic wounds, and proposes chronotherapeutic strategies aligning interventions with endogenous rhythms.

papers.title: Visual Environmental Interventions and Preoperative Sleep: The Role of Curtain Color in Surgical Patients.
papers.summary: In a prospective randomized study of 190 patients undergoing elective thoracic surgery, light-colored ward curtains (beige/light blue) were associated with better preoperative sleep quality compared to dark-colored curtains, as measured by subjective questionnaires and actigraphy. Multivariable analyses indicated that curtain color remained independently associated with both subjective and objective sleep outcomes.

papers.title: Time-frequency EEG markers of word boundaries in speech production.
papers.summary: Using EEG time-frequency analysis and source localization, the study compared word-boundary and within-word syllable transitions in adults producing pseudoword pairs. It found differential recruitment of left and right inferior frontal and left superior temporal sources, with right inferior frontal theta/beta synchronization at word transitions and left superior temporal alpha suppression at word onset.

papers.title: Salience network orchestrates large-scale brain dynamics during target detection: Insights from an EEG dFNC study.
papers.summary: The study used EEG-based dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) during a visual oddball task to examine large-scale network dynamics in target detection. It revealed a three-stage filtering-integration-regulation framework with early salience network involvement, later frontoparietal control hub shift, and salience network engagement predicting P300 amplitude and latency.

papers.title: Interictal electric source imaging with open-source software and routine low-density electroencephalography: A systematic comparison of four inverse methods in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.summary: Interictal electrical source imaging using open-source Brainstorm and routine low-density EEG in 79 drug-resistant epilepsy surgery patients compared four inverse methods at spike half-rising phase and peak. sLORETA at half-rising phase achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (81.0%) and remained robust in extratemporal, nonlesional MRI, and stereo-EEG subgroups.

papers.title: Arytenoid Asymmetry in Patients with Moderate-to-High Risk of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
papers.summary: This retrospective chart review compared arytenoid asymmetry (AA) during phonation in 64 patients at moderate-to-high risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) versus 54 controls. It found significantly higher AA prevalence in the OSA-risk group (OR=10.0, 95% CI 3.53-28.57), with all three asymmetry signs more prevalent, but no significant correlation with hoarseness.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of fNIRS-Based Neurovascular Coupling Research: Methodological Landscape and Translational Considerations for Spaceflight.
papers.summary: This PRISMA 2020 systematic review synthesized 66 fNIRS studies of neurovascular coupling in healthy adults, finding that cognitive paradigms, prefrontal cortex focus, and single stressors predominated, but no studies combined spaceflight-relevant stressors or validated fNIRS for spaceflight, limiting translation to space missions.

papers.title: Electronic media exposure and neurodevelopment in children under 5 years of age: an updated evidence-based narrative review.
papers.summary: An evidence-based narrative review synthesized 21 original studies, 12 reviews, and 4 guidelines on electronic media exposure and neurodevelopment in children under 5. It reported associations between excessive early screen exposure and language delays, attention/executive function impairments, socioemotional difficulties, sleep disturbances, reduced motor activity, and reduced white matter integrity in language pathways.

papers.title: Tai Chi modulates resting alpha and theta EEG rhythms in female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence during compulsory detoxification.
papers.summary: In a 6-month randomized trial with 32 female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence, both Tai Chi and routine physical rehabilitation reduced resting alpha and theta EEG power across multiple cortical regions. Acutely, Tai Chi elicited higher alpha and theta power in widespread regions compared to treadmill exercise, suggesting greater cortical relaxation and internal focus.

papers.title: The Circadian System and Chronic Kidney Disease Risk: Epidemiological Evidence.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 34 studies examining associations between circadian rhythm determinants (shift work, artificial light at night, melatonin, chronotype, social jetlag, insomnia, sleep duration) and chronic kidney disease risk. Consistent evidence linked shift work, evening chronotype, prolonged social jetlag, and both short and long sleep duration to elevated CKD risk.

papers.title: Clinical risk stratification of stroke caregiver distress: an interpretable nonlinear model of caregiving-load categories.
papers.summary: This multicenter cross-sectional study developed an interpretable XGBoost model using six predictor domains to stratify high psychological distress among 506 stroke caregivers. The model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.890, with role burnout, active coping, and perceived social support as top predictors, and interaction plots suggesting load-dependent associations.

papers.title: A Comparative Randomized Crossover Pilot Study Comparing Male External Urine Collection Devices in Home Settings.
papers.journal: Journal of wound, ostomy, and continence nursing : official publication of The Wound, Ostomy and Continence Nurses Society
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover pilot study of 15 community-dwelling older men requiring nocturnal urine management, a male external catheter with vacuum-assisted collection was compared to a standard condom catheter. The study device showed comparable urine capture rate (98.5% vs. 98.1%) and safety, with strong participant preference for the external collection device (86.7%).

papers.title: Effects of Esketamine on Postoperative Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Scores in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Radical Resection for Colorectal Cancer.
papers.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
papers.summary: This randomized placebo-controlled trial investigated intravenous esketamine during laparoscopic radical resection for colorectal cancer. Esketamine significantly reduced postoperative HADS anxiety and depression scores on days 1 and 3, lowered 24-hour interleukin-6 levels, and improved patient satisfaction compared to control.

papers.title: Moderators of the Effects of Telehealth Mindfulness-based Interventions for Chronic Pain: A Secondary Responder Analysis of the LAMP Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This secondary responder analysis of the LAMP randomized controlled trial tested moderating effects of gender and mental health diagnoses on outcomes of two telehealth mindfulness-based interventions (group and self-paced) versus usual care in 811 veterans with chronic pain. Both interventions showed higher improvement rates across all outcomes than usual care; in the group intervention, women had greater improvement in pain severity and depression than men, and those with anxiety diagnoses had less improvement in PTSD.

papers.title: Circadian-Inspired Hydrogel Moisture Electricity Generation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a circadian-inspired hydrogel moisture electric generator that uses diurnal temperature-moisture fluctuations to drive reversible internal water redistribution and sustained electricity generation. The device delivered a short-circuit current density of 75 µA cm−2, open-circuit voltage of 0.4–1 V, and power density of 16 µW cm−2, maintaining performance over 57 days.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and exploratory serum biomarker findings in vestibular migraine: a cross-sectional case-control study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional case-control study characterized clinical features and explored serum biomarkers in 145 patients with vestibular migraine and 50 healthy controls. Female sex, higher BMI, and positive family history were associated with vestibular migraine; serum CGRP and GDF-15 levels were associated with case status, with exploratory AUCs of 0.794 for CGRP, 0.898 for GDF-15, and 0.927 for their combination.

papers.title: Utidelone-associated chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: an evidence-stratified narrative review of mechanisms, risk identification, and management strategies.
papers.summary: This evidence-stratified narrative review synthesizes mechanisms, risk factors, and management of utidelone-associated chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), highlighting that peripheral neuropathy occurs in 59% of patients receiving utidelone plus capecitabine (grade 3: 22%) versus 8% (grade 3: <1%) with capecitabine alone. It proposes a practical management framework and distinguishes utidelone-specific evidence from extrapolated taxane/platinum findings, noting limited direct mechanistic data except a mouse study linking allodynia to TRPA1 upregulation and oxidative stress.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
